tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Portal Utilitas is: a Next.js 14 multi-tenant cashier portal for Indonesian utility payments (PDAM water, PLN electricity, BPJS insurance, Telkom, Pulsa top-ups, and Lunasin products). The README outlines the loket (cashier counter) model, role-based access, and the multi-payment batch capability that makes this portal unique.

tour.title: Database Foundation
tour.description: The baseline schema migration establishes the entire data model: 21 core tables including users, lokets, payment_requests, multi_payment_requests, transaction_events, and cashier_closings. Understanding this schema is essential because every API route and service operates against these tables. Foreign keys between lokets → payment_requests → transaction_events form the audit trail backbone.
tour.languageLesson: SQL migrations should be applied in filename order. The baseline file creates the initial schema; subsequent dated files (20260405_, 20260407_, etc.) apply incremental changes. Never modify a migration that has already been applied in production — always add a new one.

tour.title: Application Bootstrap
tour.description: next.config.js and package.json together define the runtime environment — Node.js 20+, Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, MySQL2, NextAuth.js, Midtrans, and OpenTelemetry are the key dependencies. The nixpacks.toml configures the Railway.app build pipeline for deployment, while tailwind.config.ts defines the UI design system tokens used by every component.

tour.title: Edge Middleware & Auth
tour.description: The Next.js Edge middleware runs on every request before it reaches a route handler. It checks the NextAuth.js session cookie and redirects unauthenticated users to /login, protecting all /dashboard, /api (internal), /loket, /pembayaran, and other privileged routes. The instrumentation module registers OpenTelemetry tracing so every request gets a trace span.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js middleware runs in the Edge Runtime — a lightweight V8 isolate with no Node.js APIs. This means you cannot use database connections, file system access, or heavy npm packages here. Only lightweight checks like JWT validation and cookie inspection belong in middleware.

tour.title: Auth & Database Layer
tour.description: src/lib/auth.ts configures NextAuth.js with a credentials provider that validates kasir usernames and passwords from MySQL and populates the session with user role, loket assignment, and balance. src/lib/db.ts exports a shared MySQL2 connection pool used by every service module — it is the single entry point to the database across all 50+ API routes.

tour.title: Core Type Definitions
tour.description: src/types/index.ts defines the shared TypeScript interfaces used across the entire portal: User (with role kasir/supervisor/admin), Loket (counter with saldo), PaymentRequest (idempotency key, status, provider), MultiPaymentRequest, and API response types. These types are the contract between the API routes and the UI pages.

tour.title: PDAM Payment Core
tour.description: The PDAM payment route is the heart of the portal. It handles the idempotency-safe payment flow: lock with idempotency key → call PDAM API → handle PENDING_ADVICE status (when the PDAM server returns 0310) → update payment_requests table. src/lib/pdam-api.ts wraps the external PDAM HTTP server, handling retries, timeouts, and the advice callback flow for pending transactions.

tour.title: PDAM Advice & Inquiry
tour.description: When a payment enters PENDING_ADVICE state (PDAM server code 0310), the kasir must run the advice flow to confirm payment success. src/app/api/pembayaran/pdam/advice/route.ts handles GET (list pending advice transactions for a loket) and POST (execute advice for a specific transaction code). The inquiry API provides bill lookup before payment, showing outstanding amounts.

tour.title: Multi-Payment Orchestration
tour.description: The multi-payment feature allows a single API call to trigger payments across multiple providers simultaneously. The orchestrator (src/lib/multipay/orchestrator.ts) groups items by provider type, calls the appropriate adapter (PDAM or Lunasin), and aggregates results into a parent multi_payment_requests record. The API route validates the batch and dispatches it to the orchestrator.
tour.languageLesson: The adapter pattern (src/lib/multipay/providers/) lets the orchestrator treat PDAM and Lunasin payments uniformly. Each provider adapter implements the same interface: accept a MultiPaymentItem, return a standardized result. Adding a new provider (e.g., PLN) requires only a new adapter file.

tour.title: Payment Page UI
tour.description: src/app/pembayaran/page.tsx is the main kasir work screen — it hosts tabbed payment forms for all six service types. Critically, it includes the pending PDAM advice banner (checks for PENDING_ADVICE transactions on mount and shows an alert) and the multi-payment panel. This 3000+ line component shows how the portal consolidates all payment workflows into a single, efficient screen.

tour.title: App Shell & Navigation
tour.description: The application layout is composed of the AppShell (src/ui/AppShell.tsx), AppSidebar (role-based navigation with admin/supervisor/kasir visibility), and AppTopNav (shows loket name, balance, and notification bell). The root src/app/layout.tsx wraps everything in SessionProvider and ThemeProvider. Together these components define the consistent portal chrome across all 25+ pages.

tour.title: Cashier Closing & Reports
tour.description: At the end of each shift, a kasir runs the tutup-kasir (cashier closing) flow. src/lib/cashier-closing.ts aggregates all transactions for the session, computes totals by service type, records denomination counts entered by the kasir, and persists a cashier_closings record. src/lib/print-receipt.ts and src/lib/print-cashier-closing.ts send formatted ESC/POS jobs to the print-bridge local server for thermal receipt printing.

tour.title: Transaction Monitoring
tour.description: The monitoring dashboard (src/app/monitoring/page.tsx) gives supervisors and admins full visibility into all payment requests with status filtering, stuck transaction detection, and per-transaction event logs. src/lib/transaction-events.ts persists every state transition (PENDING → SUCCESS/FAILED/PENDING_ADVICE) as an event record, providing a full audit trail for each payment.

tour.title: Balance & Top-Up
tour.description: Each loket has a saldo (balance) that decreases with each payment. When balance runs low, the kasir initiates a top-up via Midtrans (src/lib/midtrans.ts), which creates a Snap payment token. After the kasir pays via the Midtrans payment page, the webhook route (src/app/api/topup/webhook/route.ts) receives confirmation and increments the loket's balance. The RBAC module (src/lib/rbac.ts) enforces which roles can top up.

tour.title: Deployment & Infrastructure
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the portal as a standalone Next.js container using a two-stage build (install+build, then copy to slim Node.js image). The nixpacks.toml configures Railway.app deployment. The print-bridge (print-bridge/server.js) is a separate Express service running locally on the kasir's Windows machine, bridging web print requests to the physical thermal printer via PowerShell or file-copy commands.
tour.languageLesson: The print-bridge solves a fundamental web limitation: browsers cannot directly drive serial/USB printers. The kasir's browser sends print data to the local Express server (localhost:3001), which then uses Windows APIs to send raw ESC/POS bytes to the thermal printer — a common pattern for web-based POS systems.
